body:
Can AI agents build your app overnight? Yes: 24 of them build mine while I sleep.
One command in Claude Code. Research agents scope my Linear tickets, build agents implement them, and by morning there is one draft PR and a Discord ping. I decide what ships.
I'm Manraj Sidhu, AI developer, and this is the real build.
Comment SWARM for the setup. Follow @manrajtalks
guide: Run a batch of AI agents overnight so that by morning you have one draft pull request to review. You need Claude Code, a ticket tracker such as Linear, a GitHub repository and a chat app such as Discord.
1. Write your work as real tickets in Linear, each with a clear description of what "done" looks like.
1. Create a Claude Code command (a saved slash command) that starts the whole run, so you only type one thing before bed.
1. Wave one: have the command launch research agents, one per ticket, that read the code and write a short plan for each ticket.
1. Wave two: have it launch build agents that each take one plan and implement it on a separate branch.
1. Merge the finished branches into a single branch and open one draft pull request on GitHub, never a direct change to your main branch.
1. Add a Discord webhook (a URL that posts a message into a channel) and have the command post the pull request link there when the run ends.
1. In the morning, read the draft pull request, run the app, and decide what ships.
Watch out: never let agents write to main, and keep the thinking (research) and the doing (build) in separate waves, so a bad plan is caught before any code is written.

```
You are helping me set up an overnight multi-agent workflow in Claude Code. I use <ticket tracker, e.g. Linear>, <code host, e.g. GitHub> and <chat app, e.g. Discord>. My project lives in <repository name>.
Build a single saved slash command called <command name> that does the following in order:
1. Fetch the open tickets labelled <label> from my tracker.
2. Wave one: start one research sub-agent per ticket. Each reads the codebase and returns a short written plan. Agents must not edit files in this wave.
3. Wave two: start one build sub-agent per plan, each working on its own branch, implementing only that plan and running the project's tests.
4. Combine the passing branches into one branch and open a single draft pull request. Never push to or merge into main.
5. Post the pull request link and a one-line summary per ticket to a <chat app> webhook.
Constraints: cap the number of agents at <maximum agents>, stop and report if tests fail, and keep all secrets in environment variables, not in the command file.
Return the command file, any setup steps I must do by hand, and a short test plan I can run on two small tickets before trusting it.
```
